newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Hundreds flee east Zairean city in fear of Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds flee east Zairean city in fear of Mobutu.

text.p: Hundreds of residents of the rebel-held eastern Zairean city of Goma fled on Wednesday, saying they feared a counter-attack by Zairean troops following the return of President Mobutu Sese Seko to his country.
Residents said they had little confidence in the ability of Zairean rebels to defend the city, which fell in early November.
"Twenty members of my family left for Bukavu since yesterday (Tuesday). They were afraid the arrival of Mobutu could mean the start of a new war," school headmaster Juvenal Akilimali told Reuters.

Mobutu returned to Kinshasa on Tuesday after four months in Europe for cancer treatment and pledged a positive and rapid response to Zaire's crisis. But he gave no specific idea on how he planned to respond to the revolt in the east in his absence.
"Each time that Zaire has been threatened in the past, I have never pulled back. I will never pull back," Mobutu told supporters on Tuesday in an address broadcast by state radio.
The rebels have seized a swath of territory about 500 km (300 miles) long running from north to south since October.
Some residents said they were sending their families by bus from Goma towards Butembo, 200 km (125 miles) north, and Bukavu 150 km (94 miles) south, in the hope they would escape fighting.
Workers at Goma minibus companies said people started leaving on Monday because of Mobutu's return. At least 300 people left for rebel-held Butembo on Wednesday and more for Bukavu.

The exodus was based on a mixture of rumours and half-truths on Mobutu's plans to recapture Goma and a popular belief that he still had the ability to galvanise the Zairean army, which fled from the rebels.
Residents said they believed French troops were based at Kisangani, 500 km (312 miles) northwest of Goma, and would bombard Goma from the air. They said Mobutu had sworn to kill anybody left alive.
A controlled explosion of mines on the Rwandan side of the border near Gisenyi on Tuesday contributed to the panic.
"We want to run away because we are afraid to die. We have heard in Kisangani there are many soldiers who have come from France with guns," said Christine Katengwa in Birere district.
"Everybody wants to flee. We have heard that Mobutu is going to come with a huge force," said another Goma resident.
But Goma's rebel-appointed governor said Mobutu's presence changed nothing and people would fight to defend the city.

"The (Zairean) army is not an army of the people and that is why the people don't support it. This is a people's liberation war. The people will give and the people will build," Leonard Kanyamuhanga said.
The rebels, a coalition of ethnic groups with links to Rwanda, say they want talks on a settlement with Kinshasa.
"How do we know that in a few years time the rebels won't end up as bad as the old government?" said a Goma resident, who however added that the city was calmer since the rebels took it.
